subject: accountancy

concepts.title: Single Column Cash Book
concepts.definition: A primary financial record containing a single amount column on each side that documents all incoming and outgoing cash chronologically.
concepts.key_idea: Cash receipts are recorded on the debit side and cash payments on the credit side.
question_patterns: calculate the closing balance of single column cash book
find the cash in hand at the end of the month
what is the closing cash balance
determine the balance c/d in single column cash book
calculate single column cash book for the given values

solution_steps.action: sum total debit receipts including opening cash
solution_steps.explain: total debit equals opening cash plus all cash received

solution_steps.action: deduct total cash payments to get closing cash balance
solution_steps.explain: closing balance c/d is the excess of total receipts over total payments

concepts.title: Double Column Cash Book and Bank Balance
concepts.definition: A subsidiary book equipped with distinct cash and bank columns on both debit and credit sides to register physical cash and banking activities simultaneously.
concepts.key_idea: Contra entries record mutual fund movements between cash and bank on both sides of the book.
question_patterns: calculate closing bank balance in double column cash book
find the bank balance c/d after recording deposits and payments
what is the net bank balance at the end of the period
determine the closing cash and bank balances
calculate double column cash book and bank balance for the given values

solution_steps.action: sum total bank deposits with opening bank balance
solution_steps.explain: total debit in bank column includes opening balance and all deposits

solution_steps.action: subtract total withdrawals from total bank receipts
solution_steps.explain: difference gives the closing bank balance c/d or overdraft if negative

concepts.title: Petty Cash Book and Imprest System
concepts.definition: A secondary ledger maintained by a petty cashier to account for frequent low-value disbursements funded by a predetermined float called the imprest.
concepts.key_idea: The head cashier reimburses the exact sum of verified small expenditures to restore the original imprest float.
question_patterns: calculate petty cash balance in hand at the end of the period
find the reimbursement amount needed under imprest system
what is the remaining cash balance with the petty cashier
determine the closing petty cash balance
calculate petty cash book and imprest system for the given values

solution_steps.explain: add postage, conveyance, stationery, cartage and miscellaneous disbursements

solution_steps.action: calculate the remaining petty cash balance
solution_steps.explain: closing petty balance is imprest advance minus total disbursements

concepts.title: Purchases Journal and Trade Discount
concepts.definition: A dedicated subsidiary journal used exclusively to chronicle credit purchases of trading merchandise at net invoice price.
concepts.key_idea: Only credit purchases of goods meant for resale are entered, excluding cash purchases and asset purchases.
question_patterns: calculate net amount to be entered in purchases book
find the total of purchases journal after trade discount

determine the purchases book total for credit purchases
calculate purchases journal and trade discount for the given values

solution_steps.action: calculate trade discount on gross credit purchase
solution_steps.explain: trade discount equals gross purchase value multiplied by the percentage discount

solution_steps.action: deduct trade discount to arrive at net purchase value
solution_steps.explain: purchases journal records the net invoice amount after deducting trade discount

concepts.title: Purchases Return Journal
concepts.definition: A special daybook that records items of trading goods returned to suppliers along with debit note references.
concepts.key_idea: Supported by debit notes issued to creditors for defective or non-compliant merchandise returned.
question_patterns: calculate the net value of goods returned to supplier
find the amount to be recorded in purchases return book

determine the debit note amount for returned goods
calculate purchases return journal for the given values

solution_steps.action: compute trade discount allowance on returned items
solution_steps.explain: deduct the original trade discount percentage applied at the time of purchase
net return value recorded in the purchases return journal

concepts.title: Sales Journal
concepts.definition: A subsidiary record maintained to log all credit sales of merchandise to customers based on outgoing sales invoices.
concepts.key_idea: Cash sales and sales of non-inventory assets are omitted from the sales journal.
question_patterns: calculate net sales to be entered in the sales book
find the total credit sales value after trade discount
what is the entry amount in sales journal
determine the total of sales book for the period
calculate sales journal for the given values

solution_steps.action: calculate trade discount on goods sold
solution_steps.explain: discount amount is computed as trade discount rate percentage on gross sale price
net sales amount is obtained by subtracting the trade discount from gross sales

worked_examples.solution: Applying the concept's compute chain with gross_sales_amount = 10, trade_discount_rate = 10 gives 9.0.

concepts.title: Sales Return Journal
concepts.definition: A designated daybook used to record returns of goods previously sold on credit, supported by credit notes issued to customers.
concepts.key_idea: A credit note is issued to the customer acknowledging the reduction in their payable balance.
question_patterns: calculate the net value of sales return
find the amount to be recorded in sales return book

determine the total of sales return journal
calculate sales return journal for the given values

solution_steps.action: calculate trade discount on returned goods
solution_steps.explain: apply the trade discount rate agreed upon at the time of credit sale
net sales return is gross return value less trade discount

concepts.title: Journal Proper Entries Classification
concepts.definition: A residual book of original entry utilized for transactions that cannot be accommodated within any of the specialized subsidiary journals.
concepts.key_idea: Records opening, adjustment, rectification, transfer, and miscellaneous non-cash or non-trading entries.
question_patterns: identify transactions to be recorded in journal proper
classify entries under opening, adjustment, rectification or transfer
verify whether credit asset purchase is recorded in journal proper
determine the purpose of journal proper

solution_steps.action: examine transaction type and verify if covered by special daybooks
solution_steps.explain: check if transaction is cash, bank, credit purchase of goods, credit sale of goods, or goods return

solution_steps.action: route residual transaction to journal proper
solution_steps.explain: opening balances, depreciation, credit asset transactions, rectifications, and year-end transfers belong in journal proper

concepts.title: Balancing of Ledger Accounts
concepts.definition: The periodic accounting routine of computing the total difference between debit and credit sides of an account to determine its net closing balance.
concepts.key_idea: A debit balance arises when debit total exceeds credit total; a credit balance occurs when credit exceeds debit.
question_patterns: calculate the balance of ledger account
find the balance c/d in ledger account
what is the closing balance of the account
determine whether the account has a debit or credit balance
calculate balancing of ledger accounts for the given values

solution_steps.action: compute the difference between debit and credit totals
solution_steps.explain: balance is the net difference placed on the shorter side to make both totals equal
